title: JEE Main 2026 (April 2nd, Shift 2) - Mathematics - Three Dimensional Geometry
subject: Mathematics

questions.q: Let the point A be the foot of perpendicular drawn from the point $P(a, b, 0)$ on the line $\frac{x - 1}{2} = \frac{y - 2}{1} = \frac{z - \alpha}{3}$. If the midpoint of the line segment PA is $(0, \frac{3}{4}, -\frac{1}{4})$, then the value of $a^2 + b^2 + \alpha^2$ is equal to:
questions.explain:
Let the midpoint be $M(0, 3/4, -1/4)$. Using section formula, coordinates of A are $2M - P = (-a, \frac{3}{2} - b, -\frac{1}{2})$.
Since A lies on the line: $\frac{-a - 1}{2} = \frac{\frac{3}{2} - b - 2}{1} = \frac{-\frac{1}{2} - \alpha}{3} = t$.
Direction ratios of the line are $\vec{d} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{PA} = -2a\hat{i} + (\frac{3}{2} - 2b)\hat{j} - \frac{1}{2}\hat{k}$. Since $PA \perp \vec{d}$, $\vec{PA} \cdot \vec{d} = 0 \implies -4a + \frac{3}{2} - 2b - \frac{3}{2} = 0 \implies b = -2a$.
Substitute $b$ into the line equation for $A$: $\frac{-a-1}{2} = \frac{3/2 - (-2a) - 2}{1} \implies 2a - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{-a-1}{2} \implies 4a - 1 = -a - 1 \implies a = 0$. So $b = 0$.
The parameter $t = \frac{-0-1}{2} = -\frac{1}{2}$. Then $\frac{-1/2 - \alpha}{3} = -\frac{1}{2} \implies \alpha = 1$.
Therefore, $a^2 + b^2 + \alpha^2 = 0 + 0 + 1 = 1$.
